action: Apply vendor fixes for Cisco BroadWorks, Barracuda ESG, Outlook, Chromium browsers and Openwave Webtop, starting with internet-exposed systems, and check whether they were compromised before patching. Federal due dates: Barracuda Nov 13, others Nov 24.
exec: Official confirmation of active exploitation in common enterprise products sets a patching deadline for US federal agencies and a benchmark for others.
plain: US cyber agency CISA added six flaws to its list of weaknesses that attackers are actively using. They affect Cisco phone-system software, Barracuda email filtering devices, Microsoft Outlook and Google Chrome.

key_findings: CISA added six CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on evidence of active exploitation.
Products are Cisco BroadWorks (XXE), Barracuda ESG and other Barracuda products (auth bypass and OS command injection), Microsoft Outlook, Google Chromium and Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder.
The catalog notes the two Barracuda flaws can be chained: an unauthenticated config import followed by root-level command injection.
Catalog due dates are November 13 for the Barracuda flaws and November 24 for the other four.
Binding Operational Directive 26-04 applies to federal civilian agencies and also requires checking for compromise before the patch was applied.
recommendations: Prioritise rapid remediation of KEV-listed flaws on publicly exposed assets.
Check whether threat actors compromised a system before the patch was applied.
Apply vendor mitigations, or stop using the product if none are available.
Use risk-based vulnerability management and treat KEV entries as a priority even outside the federal government.

summary: The six additions are an XML external entity flaw in Cisco BroadWorks, an authentication bypass and a command injection in Barracuda Email Security Gateway, the Outlook zero-day, the Chrome zero-day and a flaw in Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder. Federal deadlines run to November 24.
title: CISA adds six exploited flaws to KEV: Cisco BroadWorks, Barracuda ESG, Outlook, Chrome, Openwave

validation.note: Reviewed against the original CISA document.
